FIRST APPEAL AND CONSEQUENTLY BE PLEASED TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 03-03-2018 PASSED BY LEARNED II ADDL. CIVIL JDUGE (SR.DN) AND MACT KALABURAGI IN MVC NO.194/2016 AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION TO RS.12,12,000/- PAYABLE WITH INTEREST AT THE RATE OF 9% PER ANNUM.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  MFA No. 201001 of 2018  JUDGMENT

2 This is petitioners' appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act')
seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of Smt. Surekha in a motor vehicles accident dated 26.06.2015.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. Petitioners are the husband and daughter of deceased-Surekha.

It is the case of the petitioners'
that on 26.06.2015 at about 1:15 p.m. deceased was travelling in an auto rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-32-4963 ('offending vehicle' for short).
On Aland-Jeerolli road, near Ajamatulla Khadri Devara Hola, due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the excel of the offending vehicle cut and it turned turtle.
Surekha sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
As the driver, owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Respondent No.1 remained ex parte.

5. Respondent No.2 filed written statement disputing that accident occurred due to rash or driving of the offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the deceased and also that petitioners were dependent on her.

Since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence,
respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.

7. Petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and Exs.P1 to 6 are marked.
8.
Respondent No.2 has not led any oral evidence, but with consent got marked copy of the insurance policy as ExR1.

9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.10,88,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

10. The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount awarded  No.
 1. Love and affection Rs.50,000/-
 2. Funeral expenses & Rs.15,000/-
 transportation charges  3. Loss of dependency Rs.10,08,000/-
 4. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
11. Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.

Santosh S/O Rantu Rathod And Ors vs Sri. Manojkumar S/O. Saibanna And Ors on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165146603/
3 12.

During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the Tribunal has erred in considering the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- p.m. and failed to add future prospects.
No compensation is granted under the head loss of consortium.
The interest awarded also on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
13. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

14. Heard arguments and perused the records.
15.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the deceased died due to the injuries sustained in the said accident has attained finality.
16. Based on the evidence placed on record, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the deceased as 21 years and multiplier 18.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal is justified in considering the income on notional basis.
Since the accident is of the year 2015, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.8,000/- p.m. instead of Rs.7,000/- p.m.
However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects.
Since the deceased was aged less than 40 years,
as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma's case)
, 40% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.
Therefore, the income is required to be taken at Rs.11,200/-.
Since there are two dependents 1/3rd deduction towards her personal and living expenses is correct.
With these components, loss of dependency is Rs.11,200 x 12 x 18 x 2/3 = Rs.16,12,800/- as against Rs.10,08,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
As husband and daughter of deceased, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e., Rs.80,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
Therefore, separate compensation granted in a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head loss of love and affection is disallowed.
18. The Tribunal has correctly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses (including transportation charges).

19. Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.17,22,800/- as against Rs.10,88,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:

Amount
awarded

To this extent, the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) Appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.17,22,800/-
as against Rs.10,88,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum.

(iii) Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest at 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of this order (minus the compensation already paid/deposited).
(iv) Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
